suppose:1.en: The market vendor slid a bowl of tea toward me without a word. I had not ordered it. I looked around for Grey Crow but saw only strangers. I *suppose* someone had told her I would come here tonight — but only Ali knew my route. I stared at the bowl and did not drink.

health:1.en: The signal led me to a small stall selling herbal drinks. A sign read: 'Good *health* starts with clean air.' Below it, in tiny coded script, was a message only I could read. It listed four names. Mine was third. My hands stayed steady but my mind was already running through exits.

health:1.line: 'They use the word *health* as a code for their next target,' Grey Crow said.

mean:1.en: Zero stepped out from behind a silk curtain at the edge of the market. 'You followed the lantern,' Zero said. 'What do you think that *means*?' I said nothing. In this city, a blinking light could mean a warning, a trap, or a hand reaching out. I had not decided which one yet.

mean:1.hook: Zero smiled — and the market lights cut to black.
mean:1.line: 'Every coded sign here *means* something, if you know how to look,' Zero said.

derive:1.en: The night market hummed with stolen frequencies. Grey Crow pressed a small device to the wet iron post. 'You can *derive* power from the city's own signal grid,' he said. The device lit up green. Somewhere above, a hidden antenna began to turn.

research:1.en: Grey Crow found me crouched behind a noodle cart. 'Your *research* into the coded graffiti is too close to the truth,' he said quietly. Around us, the market crowd moved without looking up. A red drone hovered one block away, its camera lens locked on our position.

author:1.en: A name surfaced in the signal stream: the *author* of Harbor City's master encryption key. Grey Crow read it twice and said nothing. Ali looked at me, jaw tight. The name belonged to someone we had trusted for months, someone still buying fish at the stall three meters away.

turn:2.en: Ali said to follow the blue lanterns and *turn* right at the fish market corner. I did. The alley behind was empty except for a metal box welded to the wall, its lock already broken. Inside was a folded strip of film with six frames — each one a different face. I knew two of them.

turn:2.hook: One of the faces was looking straight at the camera — smiling.
turn:2.line: '*Turn* right, walk fast, and do not look back at the market.'

less:2.hook: Four numbers, and suddenly every exit felt watched.
less:2.line: '*Less* text means someone already knows you will understand.'

information:2.en: A cracked screen glowed under a noodle cart. Someone had taped a data chip to its base. I pried it free. Grey Crow had warned me: in Harbor City, raw *information* was worth more than any weapon. I slipped it into my coat and kept walking, eyes forward.

information:2.hook: Behind me, boots splashed through puddles — getting closer.
information:2.line: '*Information* like this gets people disappeared,' Grey Crow had said.

paragraph:2.en: The wall beside the tea stall was covered in coded graffiti. Most was noise. But one short *paragraph* near the drain pipe was different — clean lines, deliberate spacing. Ali grabbed my sleeve. 'That wasn't there this morning.' Someone had written a warning in plain sight, hidden inside a city of symbols.

paragraph:2.line: 'Read that *paragraph* again — the last line changed.'

look:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a broken compass at the edge of the lantern market. Its *look* was ordinary — dull metal, scratched glass — but the needle spun in patterns, not north. Ali said nothing. She only watched the crowd. Something about that compass was coded, and I had ten minutes to read it.

look:2.hook: The needle stopped — pointing straight at Zero.
look:2.line: 'Don't let its *look* fool you; it never points to north.'

benefit:2.en: Zero stepped from the shadow of a silk stall and offered me a dry smile. 'Work with me tonight. There is real *benefit* in it for you — safe passage out of the east docks.' I said nothing. Grey Crow had told me Zero never offered a deal unless he needed something first.

benefit:2.hook: Safe passage — or a neat trap with a ribbon on it.
benefit:2.line: 'The *benefit* to you is simple: you walk away clean.'

contain:2.line: 'Whatever you do, don't let it *contain* any heat.'

direction:2.en: The signal came through my earpiece as static, then three short tones. Grey Crow's voice followed, low and clipped: 'Switch *direction*.' I was heading toward the clock bridge. I stopped, turned, and took the alley behind the salt vendors instead. Thirty seconds later, two figures crossed the bridge where I had just been standing.
direction:2.cnHint: 灰鸦通过耳机指令我改变____，让我避开了尾随者。
direction:2.hook: Those two figures paused and scanned the crowd — hunting.

attach:2.en: The package sat on the wet counter of a closed dumpling stall, wrapped in brown paper. Zero had found us first.

attach:2.hook: Somewhere in the crowd, Zero was already watching the signal move.

actually:2.hook: The signal was still live, and someone else was already listening.
actually:2.line: 'This is *actually* a warning, not a map.'

themselves:2.en: I moved through the market stalls, watching the vendors. They spoke in clipped, careful syllables, never finishing a sentence aloud. The traders here had trained *themselves* to say everything in half-words — the other half lived in the encrypted static between signs.

themselves:2.hook: One vendor's eyes locked on mine, and he stopped mid-syllable.
themselves:2.line: 'They taught *themselves* to hide words in silence.'

person:2.en: Grey Crow left a single burned match on the wet counter of stall seven. In this city, that meant exactly one thing: someone had been erased. Not their data, not their record — the *person* themselves, pulled out of every network, every camera, every trace.

without:2.en: I found the note folded inside a hollow ceramic fish at the back of the market. Four words, printed in cold type: LEAVE NOW. Then, *without* a sender, without a seal — just blank space where a name should have been, loud as a shout in the rain.

without:2.line: 'You got a warning *without* a name — that means run.'

among:2.en: Ali crouched at the edge of the canal and pointed. Dozens of paper lanterns drifted on the black water. *Among* them, one burned blue instead of orange. Blue meant a dead-drop. Someone had placed a message here for me, hidden in plain sight, floating past indifferent eyes.

among:2.line: '*Among* all those lights, only the blue one matters.'

He tapped a freshly inked section near the north gate — a new corridor, unmarked on any public chart, cut through what used to be a dead-end alley.

start:2.en: Grey Crow met me under the lantern pole at the market entrance and handed me a data card without ceremony. 'This is where it all began,' he said. The card held a single audio file — a broadcast fragment from three years ago, the *start* of every coded signal Zero had sent since.
start:2.cnHint: 灰鸦交给我一张卡片，里面存有一切暗号的____。
start:2.hook: The voice in the recording was one I already knew.
start:2.line: 'Find the *start* of the signal chain and you find the source.'

sentences.en: 'This is where it all began,' he said.

however:2.en: The stall owner swore he had seen nothing unusual near the north gate all week. His shop log showed quiet, steady sales — tea, dried fish, circuit tape. *However*, the mud on the side path told a different story: boot tracks, heavy and close together, pressed deep into the soft ground just last night.

however:2.hook: The tracks led straight under the locked service door.
however:2.line: '*However* calm it looks, the ground does not lie.'

sentences.en: The stall owner swore he had seen nothing unusual near the north gate all week.

human:2.en: The night market hummed with vendors and smoke. Ali pressed a cracked data-chip into my hand. 'This fell from Zero's coat,' she whispered. On it, one file: a list of names — every one tagged NOT *HUMAN*. My pulse spiked. What were they, if not us?

human:2.line: 'Every name here is marked NOT *HUMAN* — so what are we?'

large:2.en: Grey Crow met me beneath the neon fish stalls, rain hammering the iron roof. He unrolled a *large* paper map — rare, physical, impossible to hack. Red circles marked six points across Harbor City. 'Zero moves tonight,' he said, tapping the widest circle. 'We have one hour.'
large:2.cnHint: 灰鸦展开一张____的纸质地图，标出了零点今晚的行动范围。
large:2.hook: The widest red circle was drawn around my building.
large:2.line: 'A *large* map — old-school, unhackable, and it says you're the target.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow met me beneath the neon fish stalls, rain hammering the iron roof.

view:2.en: I climbed the old signal tower at the edge of Harbor City's night market. From up here, the *view* of a thousand glowing stalls stretched below like a living circuit board. Grey Crow had told me: the message was hidden somewhere in that light. I just had to find it.
view:2.cnHint: 我爬上信号塔，试图从高处的____中找到隐藏的信息。
view:2.hook: One light blinked in a pattern no one else had noticed.
view:2.line: 'The *view* from above never lies — look for the odd light out.'

social:2.en: Ali handed me a cracked data-chip. 'Every *social* broadcast in the market runs through this node,' she said quietly. I pressed it into my scanner. Hundreds of voices, coded and layered, filled my ears at once. Zero's signal was buried somewhere inside — I was sure of it.

social:2.hook: One voice repeated a single word, over and over, in perfect silence.
social:2.line: 'The *social* network here hides more secrets than the police ever guessed.'

sentences.cn: 我把它插进扫描仪。

sentences.en: Zero's signal was buried somewhere inside — I was sure of it.
sentences.cn: 零点的信号一定就埋在某个地方——我确信无疑。

skill:2.en: The lock on the back gate of stall forty-seven was old, but clever. Grey Crow watched as I worked. 'Pure *skill*,' he said, with something close to approval. The mechanism clicked open. Inside, a folded paper waited on an empty shelf — the kind of message people used before signals existed.

skill:2.hook: The paper held only four words, and my name was the last.
skill:2.line: 'That *skill* of yours just opened a door Zero thought was sealed.'

job:2.en: Ali spread the map across the noodle stall's wet counter. 'Our *job* tonight is simple,' she said, tracing a red line with one finger. 'Find the drop point before Zero does.' Simple, she called it. The drop point was somewhere inside a market of ten thousand strangers.
job:2.cnHint: 阿里解释了我们今晚的____：在零点之前找到那个交接地点。
job:2.hook: The red line on the map ended at a stall that sold nothing.
job:2.line: 'Our *job* is to reach that point first — every second counts now.'

sentences.en: 'Our *job* tonight is simple,' she said, tracing a red line with one finger.

business:2.en: The tea seller at stall twelve had been in this market for thirty years. I asked about the locked room behind his counter. 'Not your *business*,' he said, eyes steady. But his hand moved to cover something small and flat on the shelf — and that small move told me everything I needed.
business:2.cnHint: 茶摊老板告诉我那间上锁的房间不是我的____，但他的举动出卖了他。
business:2.hook: Whatever lay on that shelf, someone wanted it badly enough to kill.
business:2.line: 'That room is my *business* alone — walk away while you still can.'

sentences.en: I asked about the locked room behind his counter.
sentences.cn: 我问起他柜台后面那间上锁的房间。

sentences.cn: 但他的手移向架子上某个小而扁平的东西——就是那个细微的动作，告诉了我一切。

eat:2.en: Grey Crow sat across from me at a street stall, pushing food around his plate. 'You have to *eat*,' he said, without looking up. 'Long night ahead.' Under his bowl, half hidden by a paper napkin, lay a key — old brass, no label. He said nothing more. He never did.
eat:2.cnHint: 格雷·克劳催我____，却悄悄在碗底藏了一把神秘的钥匙。
eat:2.hook: The key fit no lock I had ever seen — yet.
eat:2.line: '*Eat* something now; once we move, there will be no stopping.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow sat across from me at a street stall, pushing food around his plate.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦坐在街边摊的对面，把盘子里的食物拨来拨去。

sentences.en: 'You have to *eat*,' he said, without looking up.

healthy:2.en: The medical stall near the east gate looked ordinary — bright lights, clean shelves. But every price was wrong by exactly one digit. Ali leaned close. 'A *healthy* shop with bad numbers is a shop with two sets of books,' she whispered. Behind the counter, a second screen glowed with data that had nothing to do with medicine.
healthy:2.cnHint: 一家看似____的医疗摊位账目有误，暗藏着另一套秘密数据。
healthy:2.hook: The second screen showed names — and mine was near the top.
healthy:2.line: 'A *healthy* front is the oldest trick; check what they hide behind it.'

sentences.cn: 东门附近的医疗摊位看起来很普通——明亮的灯光，干净的架子。

sentences.en: But every price was wrong by exactly one digit.

sentences.cn: 阿栗凑近了。

place:2.en: Grey Crow's message was three words: find the *place*. No address, no map marker — just those three words on a scrap of foil tucked inside my scanner case. I had walked this market a hundred times. Only one spot had no stall, no seller, no light. A gap in the grid. That had to be it.
place:2.cnHint: 格雷·克劳的纸条只写了三个字：找到那个____。
place:2.hook: The gap in the grid was exactly one person wide, and someone was already standing in it.
place:2.line: 'This *place* was left empty on purpose — someone planned for us to come.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow's message was three words: find the *place*.
No address, no map marker — just those three words on a scrap of foil tucked inside my scanner case.
sentences.cn: 纸箔上没有地址，没有地图标记——就这三个字，塞在我扫描仪盒子里面。

lot:2.line: 'A *lot* of clues, all pointing at the same door.'
